name: Zenn Foulhoof
summary: East of Dolanaar, Zenn Foulhoof asks travelers for forest reagents. The night elves watch him closely.

sections.title: A Schemer in the Woods
sections.body: Zenn Foulhoof keeps a place just outside Dolanaar, where the night elves tolerate him under watch. Most satyrs serve demonic masters and attack openly, but Zenn offers a friendly face. He says he has changed, or asks to trade for nightsaber fangs, strigid owl feathers, and webwood spider silk. Gullible youths gather the ingredients he needs for foul rituals. Dolanaar's council will not let him act unchecked. They order travelers to feed him corrupted forest fruit, humiliating him by turning the scheming satyr into a harmless frog for a time.

faq.q: Why isn't Zenn Foulhoof immediately attacked by the night elves?
aliases: why don't night elves kill zenn
faq.answer: Zenn Foulhoof keeps a friendly face and has not openly committed atrocities on the World Tree. Dolanaar's council watches him and chooses public humiliation over an immediate death sentence.

faq.q: What happens when you feed Zenn the corrupted cones and berries?
faq.answer: Dolanaar's elders order the corrupted fruit as penance for Zenn's misdeeds. The punishment's result appears when he eats it.

Satyrs were night elves who became horned, cloven-hoofed fiends during the War of the Ancients after pledging service to the Burning Legion. Most are deeply corrupted and violently hostile to their uncorrupted kin.

angles.text: As a night elf, seeing a satyr lounging on Teldrassil's sacred boughs insults Elune and the spirits of the wild. Satyrs have betrayed kaldorei heritage.
As a druid, you may see Zenn's tampering with wild reagents and spreading corrupting taints as an offense against Cenarion teachings, which seek to keep Teldrassil pristine.
